clauses.reason: The operative clause says the President does "do order that the said Plastering and Lathing Contracting Chapter be and it is hereby approved", approving the chapter and modifying the earlier approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry (approved January 31, 1934, as the order recites) to cover the supplemented code. Both effects are section 3(a) approvals with no stated period or condition. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) repealed the provisions of Title I delegating power to the President to "approve or prescribe codes of fair competition" and "providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed"; the resolution states no effective date other than its approval ("Approved, June 14, 1935."), so the approval stopped operating on June 14, 1935. Under section 3 of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) an approved code had legal effect only through 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunctions and 3(f) misdemeanor penalties, all of which the repeal removed. Schechter (SUPPLEMENT:SCHECHTERJDG, May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. The earlier approval of the Construction Industry code is a separate order outside this claim; this clause ends only the approval and modification made here.

research_rationale:
Identity and page check: the held text for EO 6750B is the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 362526), registered as grade mirror_transcription (not an original). Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2025-10-09T07:44:35Z whose heading names Executive Order 6750B, whose date (June 27, 1934) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. The WPA 1944 list row (1934 June 27 p.582: Code of Fair Competition for the Plasteringand Lath ing Contracting Division of the Construction Industry approved. XII NRA Codes 487.) confirms the order's date and subject. The order approves a code of fair competition under section 3(a) of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, so the reviewed shared analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and review-shared/ADJUDICATION.json) applies: a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935 by statutory repeal (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2); Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date. No inventory correction was needed: the one machine clause is the operative paragraph, which approves the chapter and modifies the earlier approval of the Construction Industry code.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Plastering and Lathing Contracting Chapter of the Code of Fair Competition for the Construction Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935: the Court held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization for every section 3 code approval, not as this order's end; the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 3; the provisions described were repealed on June 14, 1935 (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2).
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3 (48 Stat. 195, June 16, 1933): under 3(a) the President approved codes and could impose conditions of approval; under 3(b), 3(c) and 3(f) an approved code's provisions became standards of fair competition enforceable by injunction and as misdemeanors. These are the legal effects that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: enactment date of NIRA section 5; S.J. Res. 113 (June 14, 1935) limited the exemption by proviso; the held text does not settle the proviso's effect on past action.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 5 exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under Title I and any complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days thereafter; any exemption for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.
